title: A dynamic body-selective area localizer for use in fMRI
author: Ross, de Gelder, et al.

steps.title: Prepare participant and scanner
steps.instruction: Recruit 26 adults (age 18–27, mean 21.28 ± 2.11 years, 15 female) and install them comfortably in the MRI scanner; restrict head motion with comfortable but tight padding; back‑project stimuli onto a screen positioned at the back of the scanner bore; attach a mirror to the head‑coil so participants can view the screen; instruct participants to keep their gaze at the centre of the screen.

substeps.instruction: Recruit 26 adults (age 18–27, M = 21.28 y, SD = 2.11, 15 female).
Install participant comfortably in scanner.
Restrict head motion using comfortable but tight padding.
Position stimulus screen at the back of the scanner bore and attach a mirror to the head‑coil for viewing.
Instruct participant to maintain gaze at the centre of the screen.

steps.title: Present stimuli and instruct participant
steps.instruction: Project the experimental video clips onto the screen; participants view the stimuli via the mirror; remind them before the main experiment to pay careful attention, to look at the central fixation cross, and to keep their head still throughout.

substeps.instruction: Back‑project video stimuli onto the screen.
Ensure participants view the screen through the mirror.
Remind participants before the main run to: (i) pay careful attention to the stimuli, (ii) look at the central fixation cross, and (iii) keep their head still.

steps.title: Run first‑level GLM analysis
steps.instruction: For each participant create a general linear model with one predictor for body images and one for non‑body images, add the luminance‑change measure (video‑clip motion) as a covariate, include the six head‑motion parameters as regressors of non‑interest, estimate the model, and compute the Body > Non‑Human contrast between individual parameter estimates.

substeps.instruction: Create GLM with two predictors: body and non‑body conditions.
Add luminance‑change (video‑clip motion) as a covariate.
Add the six head‑motion parameters as regressors of non‑interest.
Estimate the model for each participant.
Compute the Body > Non‑Human contrast from the individual parameter estimates.

steps.title: Perform second‑level group analysis
steps.instruction: Take the first‑level contrast images to a second‑level random‑effects ANOVA, apply a voxel‑wise threshold of p < 0.05 family‑wise error (FWE) corrected, enforce a minimum cluster extent of 10 voxels, and label peak activations using the Harvard‑Oxford cortical and sub‑cortical atlases in FSLview.

substeps.instruction: Enter contrast images into a second‑level random‑effects ANOVA.
Threshold statistical maps at p < 0.05 FWE‑corrected (voxel level).
Apply a cluster‑extent threshold of ≥10 voxels.
Determine anatomical locations of peak activations with the Harvard‑Oxford cortical and sub‑cortical atlases via FSLview.

steps.title: Assess individual activation thresholds
steps.instruction: Examine each participant’s activation maps using three statistical thresholds: (i) p < 0.001 uncorrected, (ii) p < 0.05 FWE‑corrected, and (iii) p < 0.05 uncorrected (as in the reference), noting the proportion of participants showing activation in each region at each threshold.

substeps.instruction: Inspect individual maps at p < 0.001 uncorrected.
Inspect individual maps at p < 0.05 FWE‑corrected.
Inspect individual maps at p < 0.05 uncorrected (reference threshold).
Record the percentage of participants with activation in each region for each threshold.
